To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL‐2 is a key cytokine in promoting Th differentiation and that STAT3, IRF4, and AP‐1 proteins are important in the regulation of T‐cell differentiation.
STAT proteins and the AP‐1 family protein IRF4 cooperate in a complex that broadly influences T‐cell differentiation.

STAT proteins are critical for the differentiation of T‐helper cell subsets and the generation of memory T cells and that the STAT3‐IRF4‐AP‐1 complex regulates T‐cell differentiation, survival, and function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying T‐cell differentiation and the complex interactions of transcription factors that mediate the biology of T cells.
the complex interactions of transcription factors that are critical to mediating the biology of cytokine signaling in T cells.

how transcription factors and their cofactors interact in the context of T‐cell differentiation, and how this knowledge can be applied in the development of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of autoimmune diseases and cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the complex interactions of transcription factors, cytokines, and epigenetics are critical in mediating cytokines' biology in T cells.
the complex interactions between cytokines, transcriptional factors, and epigentics play a crucial role in the differentiation of Th cells.
IL‐2 is a master regulator of Th‐cell development and function, and its role is not limited to the regulation of Treg cells, but it is a key regulator for Th1 and Th17 cells as well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the STAT and IRF4‐AP‐1 complexes are important for Th differentiation, and that the balance between STAT and AP‐1 proteins is important in determining whether Th1 or Th2 cells will be generated.

IL‐2, which is a key regulator of T‐cell homeostasis, can also promote the differentiation of multiple Th cell subsets and is an important regulator of the balance between Th1, Th17, and Treg cell differentiation.

the complex interaction of transcription factors in the regulation of T‐helper cell differentiation is critical for normal immune function and that the dysregulated activity of these factors may contribute to the development of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cytokines, such as IL‐2, can have multiple and opposing roles in the differentiation of T‐helper subsets, depending on the context of the transcription factors present in the cell.
